changes: Add individual full-height door openings to existing Office Space wall segments, selectable during the Closed Outline draft; preserve openings in saved wall objects and Architecture presets.

Generate saved single-slope roofs (4 orientations), flat overhang roofs and pyramid roofs, with optional chimney, solar-panel details and roof opening; validate and preview through the existing Office Space wall panel.

Restore saved seating anchors after furniture and robot scene hydration, stand clear of chair and sofa fronts, recover robot foot elevation from upper-storey supporting surfaces, and avoid stale procedural leg poses in authored walking animation.
Add entry/last/saved per-room camera start position, a one-click save-with-confirmation action in the shared Control Switcher beside follow/distance controls; save camera pose only, not world state.
Introduce per-robot comic speech/thought bubble options for shape (rounded/oval/cloud), Digital Strip or fallback font family, all-caps and visibility, without redistributing uploaded font binaries.
Unify the Office Space wall numeric slider with the shared active-field slider beneath the focused row; add backend and regression checks for new door/roof/preset, camera, seating and comic settings.
Active infrastructure drawing Ctrl/Cmd+Z/Y/Shift+Z now undoes/redoes path vertices, freehand strokes and draft field changes rather than unrelated saved scene history.
Continuous freehand capture and adaptive path simplification preserve gestures beyond 80 raw points while saving no more than 80 validated control points.
Restore camera orbit/pan/zoom while creating infrastructure; only left scene clicks append vertices; show a temporary dashed guide from the previous vertex to the pointer.
Keep fence, hedge, road and wall controls in the existing Properties window; remove meaningless fence/wall Width setting and live-preview functional settings.
Detect a robot capsule wedged and frozen in a falling animation against edited walls/fences and return it to a last safely grounded pose and Idle.
Introduce robot head-anchored comic speech/thought overlays, using the user-supplied SVG assets without redistributing the separately uploaded proprietary font.
Extend automated tests and retain all prior assets, room sync, presets and watcher-compatible application file integrity.

Replace fragmented Finish/Undo/Cancel controls and unreadable column-wrapped status with a single full-width inline row: an accent-coloured, descriptive Save construction action, Undo and Cancel, plus a concise single-line preview status in the standard draggable Properties inspector.
Fix the 54px legacy furniture-column CSS override that squeezed drawing status and drawing mode into vertical letter stacks; keep the compact three-column property grid unchanged for normal settings.

Remove the exposed arbitrary texture/variation seed from infrastructure Properties; add actual selectable Wood, Concrete, Brick, Metal, Plaster, Marble and Granite finishes for solid walls and fences using SOLVI’s existing procedural texture generator.

Keep the deterministic internal material seed for asphalt/paving texture generation, but make roads use named surface presets and walls/fences use visible named finishes; validate infraTexture on the backend with legacy defaults.

Retain unsaved 3D live previews, single-line, polyline and freehand modes, existing scene persistence, undo/cancel restoration, multiplayer and avatar GLBs; test focused UI, sanitizer, backend and archive watcher consistency.

Show real generated 3D infrastructure geometry immediately after two committed ground points: textured walls, plank/mesh/rod fences, hedges, curbs, continuous paved footpaths and roads including lane markings and streetlights.

Rebuild the live construction preview when Properties values change, so dimensions, height, textures, fence spacing, road settings and smoothing are visible before saving; no pointer-following phantom line.
Keep preview geometry isolated from the saved scene and collider world; dispose temporary geometry, textures and materials between updates, and throttle freehand preview construction for WebXR.
Single-line drawing remains editable until the user chooses Finish; Cancel restores original infrastructure furniture properties and appearance, and no draft is saved or transmitted.
Add runtime-mocked drawing and preview regression tests, verify all JavaScript syntax and watcher-compatible versioned ZIP with SHA-256 for each application file.
Replace disconnected rectangular road slabs with one indexed connected ribbon surface and shared corner joins; use bounded smooth cubic paths and a continuous static road collision mesh.

Remove the separate Draw Infrastructure popup. Drawing a wall, fence, hedge, road or footpath opens the existing draggable Properties inspector with single-line, polyline and freehand choices plus Undo/Finish/Cancel.
Show only already placed drawing points instead of a ghost segment following the cursor; ensure Properties stays above the drawing shield and finished or cancelled paths release controls.
Keep brand-new paths unsaved until completed, preserving scene, multiplayer, presets and Undo behaviour. Full edited settings are retained on redraw.
Make the road lane count a whole integer from 1 to 6 in the numeric input and the single shared range slider; preserve road markings, paving materials, curbs, footpaths and streetlights.
Add an Outdoor Infrastructure drawing workflow for walls, fences, hedges, curbs, footpaths, and roads using single-line, multiline, or freehand placement.
Build deterministic, bounded roads with adjustable tarmac, lanes, one/two-way orientation, road markings, curbs, pavements and streetlights.
Create plank, mesh and metal-rod fence presets, editable plant hedges and solid perimeter walls with configurable spacing and dimensions.
Persist each infrastructure path as one scene furniture object with inspector controls, preset compatibility, multiplayer sync, undo and a static collider for structural surfaces.
Validate all new options and path coordinates in the backend, preserve original avatar assets and run syntax, checksum, version and regression tests before release.
Fix an uncommented note in js/editor.js that caused node --check to reject the full v0.2.171 deployment before tests could run.
Repair TV and monitor HLS startup: attach MediaSource before requesting the playlist, wait for HLS manifest and media metadata, and start playback only once ready.
Retry muted playback when browser autoplay rules block remote audio; preserve spatial audio and existing screen controls.
Surface failed stream playback in the in-world menu instead of leaving a black/blank monitor, and apply the same readiness handling to smart speakers.
Add a release regression that checks JavaScript syntax for every shipped JS/MJS file and tests HLS event ordering, media readiness, and playback fallback.

Give every numeric furniture and vegetation inspector parameter its own always-visible compact range slider directly beneath the corresponding number input, including orchard/forest scatter, soil, terrain and water parameters.
Keep the three-column inspector grid stable: all companion range controls are present from render time and do not insert, remove, resize or reflow other fields on focus.
Synchronise range dragging and typed numeric values in both directions through the existing debounced geometry preview, undo history, physics update and multiplayer save pipeline.
Preserve the existing floating contextual slider for transform position/rotation/scale, while avoiding redundant popovers over furniture controls.
Add regression checks for slider creation, numeric bounds, change propagation and consistent non-reflow layout.
Centre all single-seat robots on the cushion rather than the armrest, and give each sofa occupant a unique slot.
Add a persisted seatMoveMode for furniture: stand on movement or follow the furniture, including translation, rotation and physics pushes.
Keep multiple seated robots bound to their own furniture-local anchors without making the robots children of the furniture mesh.
Automatically stand occupied robots when non-stickable furniture is moved or removed, clearing sitting pose and restoring idle and physics.
Persist and validate robot seat anchors across multiplayer scene updates and remap references through realm archives.
Expand seating regressions and preserve original avatars, physics and inventory code.
Add terrain-relief support to ground and crop patches so drawn vegetation areas generate bounded height irregularity and act as elevated support surfaces for robots and XR teleport landing.
Add draw-on-ground water/lake patches with negative bowl terrain, adjustable water depth and level, freehand or parametric patch shapes, and semi-transparent wavy water surfaces.
Extend nature object editing with patch-shape controls, relief/detail parameters and lake-specific controls while preserving existing preset and saved-scene compatibility.
Add trimesh collider support for terrain furniture segments so capsules, dropped objects and teleport selection respect patch elevation instead of sinking through flat ground.

Add seeded Nature arrays as a single persistent Vegetation Area object with orchard rows, mixed forests, clustered thickets, and brushwood patches; keep the entire patch under one multiplayer object ID.
Add individually editable Shrub / Brushwood objects with adjustable height, spread, branch count, foliage clusters and shape, all compatible with the existing Nature preset gallery.

Draw orchard/forest/brushwood planting areas on the ground with the existing polygon closure, smoothing and redraw tools; expose density, spacing, species, scatter seed, cluster strength and scale variation in compact Properties.

Use bounded shared InstancedMesh batches for trunks, crowns, conifers, palms, shrubs and undergrowth rather than creating a separate mesh per plant; retain deterministic restoration and prior v0.2.165 Nature scenes.
Extend backend validation and add multi-mode deterministic scattering, geometry-budget and editor integration regression tests.
Replace dark checkerboard soil with continuous multi-scale value noise, tone mapping and sRGB output; preview vegetation edits while numeric controls change.
Replace static grass cones with a single instanced mesh of thin blades, vertex-shader wind displacement, adjustable width/strength/speed and a bounded per-plot draw budget.
Extend the tree builder with blossom trees, palm fronds and coconuts; reduce default leaf sizes and make seeded foliage clusters denser without per-leaf draw calls.
Add procedural wood bark selection, trunk noise irregularity and editable blossom colour/density, keeping earlier Nature scenes and presets readable.
Extend backend validation and add regression tests for new vegetation settings, deterministic tree generation and bounded scene geometry.

Create bounded, seed-reproducible procedural broadleaf, conifer, and orchard trees with adjustable height, trunk/leaf geometry, fruit and colours; foliage/fruit are instanced for WebXR draw-call efficiency.

Add soil/grass plots and simple crop beds using a lightweight procedural ground shader, instanced grass and vegetable rows with manual growth percentage, soil type, colours and fixed complexity budgets.
Draw ground polygons from the Add > Nature menu; auto-close the boundary on Save/Enter or click near start, with optional outline smoothing and editable saved points.
Enable tree, soil and crop configurations as account-saved presets in a new Nature gallery tab; preserve existing scene IDs and cross-client furniture updates.
Validate all new settings, numeric ranges, plot coordinates and bounded polygon sizes on the backend; no new asset dependency, watcher changes or third-party runtime library.
Move avatars beyond the selected seat footprint when standing with J, retaining yaw and synchronising the actual Rapier pose; avoid leaving standing robots inside sofas/chairs.

Replace oversized stacked audio recording label sprites with a compact, modern single canvas label displaying author/date/time and PLAY/PAUSE; activate playback by clicking the label in desktop and WebXR.
Upgrade procedural Office chair with an optional ergonomic backrest opening, optional armrests and a five-spoke wheeled pedestal base; retain four-leg variants and existing seat/preset persistence.
Centre the preset Delete SVG in its button and prevent an automatically decorated duplicate icon from shifting it.
Brighten Save Chat Portrait independently of the previously corrected robot eye-camera via sRGB offscreen output and temporary neutral portrait lights; restore scene and GPU state after capture.
Interrupt the pickup/lift animation as soon as genuine avatar locomotion begins, while preserving the object carry timer and grip; recover looping gaits from a paused one-shot state.
Capture robot eye-camera JPEGs with proper sRGB output from the offscreen render target to avoid underexposed linear colour readback.
Add procedural Office chair with seat, backrest, adjustable optional headrest and single-pedestal/four-leg bases, using existing furniture editor, presets and seat logic.
Expose independently adjustable translucent bottle liquid opacity, with a visible fill-level surface; preserve old bottle opacity and cap behaviour.
Use the supplied Delete SVG and ensure the SVG button glyph is centred horizontally and vertically in existing SOLVI icon buttons.
Inventory window uses the shared draggable-window system and displays robot portrait plus thumbnail-based item cards.
Presets become truly image-only click targets without the global automatic Add icon; name and type overlay the preview and Delete remains a corner icon.
Rebuild all supported procedural preset thumbnails using the shared dedicated offscreen renderer, with centered orthographic object bounds.
Bottles support shell opacity, hollow uncapped opening, liquid colour and 0–100% simulated fill level.
Shift+I picks up a nearby backpack or removes a worn backpack without losing its stored contents.

Keep procedural smart TV/monitor media menus in sync with the exact saved inspector channel array, including after edits, preset load and remote scene updates; refresh menu textures without breaking current video/audio when the same channel remains.
Redesign the preset gallery as image-first cards: thumbnail click directly inserts and closes, remove redundant permanent plus/Add control, and use a compact SVG delete icon over the thumbnail.
Use projected camera-space bounds to center and tightly frame procedural thumbnails in a brighter isolated render, and regenerate gallery previews for saved furniture using current geometry.
Add functional regression checks and preserve source-controlled assets; no watcher changes required.

Route smart TV, monitor and media-frame video/HLS sound through Three.js PositionalAudio attached to each display, using the existing camera/WebXR AudioListener for distance attenuation and HRTF directional panning.
Use a forward-facing sound cone with reduced rear output, preserve the on-screen mute control and mute Web Audio gain along with the video element.
Disconnect positional audio nodes when switching channels or deleting screens; keep existing channels, IPTV, mute settings and backend schema unchanged.
Include targeted spatial-audio regression tests and preserve original avatar files.
Add selectable per-display audio enabled/start-muted, persistent mute overlay, optional original-aspect playback, recorded-video looping, configurable initial channel and opt-in startup playback.
Enable copying an HTTPS HLS/MP4/WebM URL and pasting directly while a TV or monitor is selected; add without a separate clipboard button.
Add CORS-aware IPTV .m3u playlist import, bounded search results and one-click channel selection from curated country/category playlists.
Apply smart playback options to procedural TVs/monitors and in-world media frames with strict frontend/backend validation; retain saved Rantlist channels and existing avatar models.
Fix smart-screen selection in Edit Mode and WebXR; add Play buttons for saved TV, monitor and media-frame channels and handle screen cleanup safely.
Improve remote walking animation tolerance, add contextual Cmd+/ robot keyboard help derived from per-robot combat shortcut settings and an explicit wearable Take off action.
Improve procedural preset card layout and center/safely frame thumbnail captures; clicking the preview directly adds an object.
Add procedural lamps with sphere/cuboid/pyramid shades, point/spot lights, adjustable intensity/range/opacity and a physical power switch.
Add procedural speakers with named saved HTTPS media channels, spatial audio, playback by clicking in-world or selecting a channel in Properties.
Synchronise stair root and tread surface color during editing, retain collision and persistence, preserve existing avatar GLBs and scene compatibility.
Add TV, monitor and media-frame smart-channel galleries for up to 12 HTTPS HLS/MP4/WebM sources, with explicit in-world selection and return-to-menu controls.
Allow clipboard paste of validated media URLs in Properties; playback uses native HLS or bundled Hls.js when supported, without arbitrary server-side URL fetching.
Reframe new procedural preset thumbnails using geometry-bound orthographic projection; regenerate existing furniture thumbnails locally when browsing Presets.
Expose wearable attachment skeleton bone, follow-rotation choice and XYZ position/rotation offsets in object Properties; lower default backpack position and rotate back slot by 90 degrees.
Add procedural sunbed, deck chair and beach umbrella variants with compact parameters and safe compound collision; sunbed and deck chair support reclined sitting and authored lying-clip fallback.
Retain versioned browser modules, existing scene/preset structures and uploaded avatar files; validate new fields in backend and import/export paths.
Fix incoming remote procedural furniture updates by rebuilding changed geometry under the existing object ID and refreshing colliders.
Introduce five editable procedural equipment types: TV, monitor, mini computer, bin and wearable backpack; existing furniture/preset scene kinds are reused.
Use compact three-across interaction checkboxes with the consumable option next to Pickable and Follow hand rotation; clarify inventory category and size choices.
Allow TVs and monitors to select existing scene image/video sources by media ID; use account-authenticated blob loading, muted playback and offline state when unavailable.
Generate basic backpack mesh and straps with the existing wearable inventory category and front/back slots; preserve original avatar and imported model bytes.
Open bins use side-part compound colliders rather than an invisible solid spanning the opening; procedural objects remain configurable and eligible for presets.
Seat avatars on nearby compatible flat surfaces with authored Sitting clips or procedural fallback, edge-aware position and facing, and orientation retained on standing (J).
Press I while carrying a Pickable object to place it on the floor without throwing; retain O for animated projectile throws and sync drops over multiplayer.
Scene-backed inventory supports pocket tools, keys, money, phone, notepad and food, with separate consumable Eat/Use and bag-size requirements.
Attach wearable backpacks, jetpacks and parachutes to upper spine/chest bones in independent front/back slots; dropped backpacks retain their contents.
Compact inventory panel with Pockets, Wearable, Backpack tabs; validated per-object state persists through scene/room saves and realm archives.
Regression tests for geometry seating, dropped object collider state, backpack contents, storage transitions, server/archive persistence and safe release packaging.
Compact Basic Furniture properties into responsive three-across labelled numeric fields matching the dark Transform controls, with the existing contextual slider retained.
Prevent keyboard input, arrow-key stepping, robot shortcuts and camera movement from interfering with active form controls; clear held robot keys on edit focus.

Move webcam, virtual camera and recorded video into one fixed preview stage directly below the My camera header, with minimal overlay tracking and capture controls; keep recorded sharing actions in one compact row.
Use the supplied SVG Play, Pause, Stop and Record controls, replacing ambiguous text glyphs in the custom media player.

Fix blank chat video by retrieving the authenticated video blob, decoding a local preview-frame poster, and playing the direct recording instead of relying on HLS negotiation; expose codec and decode errors.
Report pose/hand landmark detection exceptions to the console and camera status without treating routine TensorFlow Lite or MediaPipe acceleration warnings as fatal.

Automated tests cover inspector layout, keyboard isolation, unified camera stage, video preview/direct playback, pending attachment thumbnails, SVG transport icons and diagnostics. Real webcam, playback and MediaPipe require browser smoke testing.

Unify Basic Furniture numeric inputs and dropdowns with the compact dark Transform inspector appearance; expose one reusable contextual slider for the currently focused numeric property without rendering a slider on every row.
Preserve numeric focus and linked slider during dimension editing; expand the contextual numeric-slider pattern across compatible Properties inspector fields.

Fix resetting or entering rotation/position on Dynamic Rapier objects by explicitly synchronising the edited rigid-body pose and clearing inherited velocities without changing ordinary gravity updates.
Fix presets spawning back at world origin for Dynamic objects: after camera-centre ground placement, also move the Rapier body to the new transform.
Fix audio-only recording null getTracks crash when both optional video streams were null; log recording exceptions to developer console and display actionable permission/device errors.

Unify webcam recordings under the single draggable My camera panel with capture status, time, audio-level meter, playback and Attach to chat / Add to scene / Place on surface / Discard actions; keep audio-only recordings in chat composer.
Retain the My camera feed during recording (no duplicate preview) and display recorded playback in the same panel; use existing window drag and position persistence.

Add five focused regressions for physics transform edits, preset placement, compact numeric inspector, null audio recording, and single camera interface. Browser/WebRTC and live Rapier gameplay require deployment testing.
Compact the Pickable, Follow hand rotation and Climbable checkboxes into a two-/three-column left-aligned grid with consistent 15px controls instead of tall full-width rows.
Place newly created procedural objects and furniture at the viewport centre projected onto the ground plane, grounding the actual mesh bounds rather than applying a fixed forward camera offset.
Add user-owned, account-persistent procedural Presets gallery with categories, search by name, object preview thumbnails, instant Add and Delete. Presets are accessible from World tools and Add menu.

Save named procedural settings (variants, dimensions, materials/colours, scale/rotation, physics and interaction flags) for furniture, Basic props, standard geometry, curves/text, ladder and non-lift stairs. New instances are independent objects with new ownership and scene IDs.

Secure Flask/SQLite /api/object-presets with per-user CRUD, bounded finite configurations, safe image previews and exclusion of unrelated uploaded assets. Exclude custom-uploaded texture presets and non-single-object lifts.

Add focused frontend regression tests for preset categories, deep-copy/no scene identity, camera-centre ground ray, scoped checkbox CSS and authenticated gallery wiring. Live browser visual/UI behaviour remains unverified.

Add per-Pickable-object Follow right-hand bone rotation checkbox. Animated metacarpal/palm orientation drives carried model rotation when enabled; opt-out preserves original orientation (useful for javelins).

Preserve hand orientation through release, with a validated optional quaternion in authoritative object-carry throw packets; save the new field through full/atomic scene, duplication and realm archives.
Subscribe to Rapier collision-start events for released objects with CCD, use world-space contact points and incoming speed to trigger head/body impact classification.
Play authored Head Hit or Hit to Body reactions on robot avatars, and one-shot matching clips on imported GLB/FBX scene models when available. No invented fallback animations.
Render brief, bounded and disposable spark lines at contact points. The ImpactEffects emitter registry is extensible for future particles; sparks are never saved or broadcast as scene objects.
Mirror eligible hit reactions and sparks with permission-checked recent projectile events, per-target deduplication and physics event expiry. No modifications to user-owned avatar GLBs.
Add focused runtime coverage for bone-rotation opt-out, contact-based hit and head classification, and network/effect integration.
Remove arbitrary numeric min/max limits from all eight Pickup & Throw inspector inputs, including Throw force >10 m/s, angles, height, delays and animation speed multipliers.
Persist finite user-entered throw values through inspector, scene serialization and backend validation; retain each field on editing and do not silently substitute 55%.
Apply throw force and aiming without old 10 m/s, 65° or 90° caps; make trajectory guidance cover longer flights and protect Rapier from unrepresentable f32 impulses.
Synchronize Lifting and Throw animation playback/timing with unrestricted positive speed multipliers; preserve ordinary avatar rate limits outside carry animations.

Percent delays remain editable without input range caps: negative values act at the beginning, values above 100% act at the clip end; reject invalid/nonfinite numbers, negative force and nonpositive speed.
655/655 JavaScript tests passed, including eight new unbounded-control regression tests; original GLB assets are unchanged.
Release archive corrected: generated Python __pycache__ / .pyc artifacts excluded; application source code and version unchanged.
Fix Release delay settings snapping to the 55% default while editing by committing valid numeric input immediately and protecting focused fields from inspector refresh.
Clamp out-of-range completed release/pickup delays to the valid 5–95% interval; preserve the last saved value for empty/invalid inputs.
Apply reliable editing to all eight per-avatar Pickup & Throw numeric controls, keeping undo history and ordinary scene persistence.
Retain v0.2.147 throw force, animation speeds, trajectory guide, procedural models and original GLB assets unchanged; five new regression tests; 647/647 JavaScript tests passed.
Adjust per-avatar Lifting and Throw animation speeds independently (0.5–3×), with pickup and release percentages remaining aligned to the resulting clip timelines.
Add a per-avatar Throw force setting (1.2–10 m/s target launch speed), applying mass-scaled forward/upward Rapier impulse after hand-height release.
Add an opt-in temporary trajectory guide with a line and landing marker calculated from the actual throw aim and launch force; truncate the prediction at Rapier geometry raycast hits or floor.
Retain Test sphere and per-avatar throw settings, preserve old saved values, and keep the preview out of scene persistence and multiplayer.
Add five regression tests for animation timing, throw impulse, ballistic path, collision checks and transient guide cleanup; 642 JavaScript tests passed.
